chapters.5.meaning: The Philistines capture the ark but cannot control God. Their idol falls, and their towns suffer.
chapters.5.lds: The older manual connects the ark’s troubles with Israel’s need to honor God.
chapters.8.summary: Samuel’s sons take bribes. Israel’s elders ask for a king. Samuel warns that kings take people, land, and goods.
chapters.9.meaning: Saul sets out to find lost donkeys. The search brings him to Samuel and a new task.
chapters.11.meaning: Saul rescues Jabesh Gilead. He then stops supporters from killing people who had opposed him.
chapters.13.summary: Jonathan attacks a Philistine post. Saul’s men begin to leave. Saul offers a sacrifice before Samuel arrives. Samuel rejects his family’s lasting rule.
chapters.13.meaning: Saul acts because he fears losing his army. Samuel says he has not kept God’s command.
chapters.15.meaning: Saul spares Agag and valuable animals. Samuel challenges his claim of obedience. The order also calls for killing children.
chapters.15.lds: Come, Follow Me asks why obedience matters more than making a religious display.
chapters.17.summary: David brings food to his brothers. He accepts Goliath’s challenge and strikes him with a sling. He then uses Goliath’s sword.
chapters.17.lds: Come, Follow Me asks how trust in God can give courage during a hard task.
chapters.20.lds: What does Jonathan risk by protecting David from his father?
chapters.23.lds: How does David respond when the town he saved may hand him over?
chapters.25.meaning: Abigail stops David from killing Nabal’s household. David accepts her correction and thanks God for her help.
chapters.26.meaning: David again has a chance to kill Saul. He takes Saul’s spear and water jug instead.
chapters.27.lds: The older manual links David’s raids with earlier commands to take the land. The raids also kill whole households.
chapters.28.summary: Saul seeks help from a woman who calls on the dead. The chapter names Samuel as the speaker who warns him of defeat.
chapters.28.lds: The older manual says the speaker was not Samuel. The chapter itself repeatedly calls him Samuel.
chapters.29.lds: Why do the Philistine leaders distrust David, even though Achish trusts him?
chapters.30.lds: Why does David share recovered goods with people who stayed behind?
chapters.31.lds: How do the people of Jabesh Gilead honor Saul after his defeat?
people.samuel.meaning: Samuel leads Israel and anoints its first two kings. His sons’ bribery helps prompt the demand for a king.
people.ichabod.meaning: His mother names him when she hears that the ark is lost. The name expresses her grief.
people.saul.meaning: Saul first rescues his people. His later jealousy and attacks on David divide his household and weaken his rule.
people.saul-servant.meaning: He suggests asking Samuel for help with the lost donkeys. His advice changes Saul’s journey.
people.nahash.meaning: Nahash demands that the men of Jabesh Gilead lose an eye before surrendering. Saul stops him.
people.jonathan-saul.meaning: Jonathan protects David despite Saul’s anger. Their friendship puts Jonathan at risk within his own family.
people.merab.meaning: Saul offers Merab to David but later gives her to Adriel. The chapter gives no words from her.
people.ishvi.meaning: Ishvi appears in Saul’s family list in chapter 14. Later lists name Saul’s sons differently.
people.agag.meaning: Saul spares Agag despite the command he received. Samuel later kills the captive king.
people.jonathan-boy.meaning: The boy gathers arrows while Jonathan sends David a hidden warning. He does not know their plan.
people.david.meaning: David gains support through courage and care. He also lies and kills families during raids.
people.moses.meaning: Samuel recalls Moses leading Israel out of Egypt. He uses this history when speaking about Israel’s new king.
people.aaron.meaning: Samuel recalls Aaron alongside Moses when telling how God brought Israel out of Egypt.
people.gideon.meaning: Samuel recalls Gideon among the leaders God sent to rescue Israel.
people.jephthah.meaning: Samuel recalls Jephthah among Israel’s earlier rescuers when asking the people to trust God.
